items.title: Mistake 1
items.text: Confusing Writing Testable Lua Code with a similarly named feature in another language or runtime. Fix: follow the version-matched reference and test the smallest example.

items.title: Mistake 2
items.text: Relying on an output order or environment capability that the language/host does not guarantee. Fix: document assumptions and make order/capabilities explicit.

items.title: Mistake 3
items.text: Skipping a boundary test or failing to check error-return values. Fix: test invalid and boundary inputs and inspect failure values.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: explain Writing Testable Lua Code without the example, predict its behavior, and name one limit. Next: Unit Testing.

content.task: Try it yourself: adapt the example to demonstrate “Writing Testable Lua Code” with a different input or boundary case. Predict the result before running it, record what you observe, and explain one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the central behavior of Writing Testable Lua Code in your own words.
Verify the result using a supported local runtime or clearly state why the host/tooling prevents a full run.
Identify a boundary case or compatibility/security limit relevant to the lesson.
hints: First identify the input, output, and any assumed runtime or host feature.
Reduce the problem to the smallest example that exposes the relevant rule.
Test one normal case and one boundary/failure case; inspect error output without leaking secrets.
